line_breaking.description: Rules for optimal event line breaking configuration

suggestion.title: Consider LINE_BREAKER for better performance
suggestion.message: Using LINE_BREAKER instead of SHOULD_LINEMERGE provides a significant boost to processing speed. SHOULD_LINEMERGE reassembles individual lines into events, while LINE_BREAKER directly delimits events.

suggestion.title: Add SHOULD_LINEMERGE = false
suggestion.message: When using a custom LINE_BREAKER, you should explicitly set SHOULD_LINEMERGE = false to prevent Splunk from attempting to reassemble lines after breaking.

suggestion.title: Consider adding event boundary settings
suggestion.message: SHOULD_LINEMERGE is enabled but no event boundary pattern is defined. Consider adding BREAK_ONLY_BEFORE, MUST_BREAK_AFTER, or BREAK_ONLY_BEFORE_DATE to define how events should be merged.

suggestion.title: DATETIME_CONFIG = NONE without event boundaries
suggestion.message: When DATETIME_CONFIG is set to NONE, Splunk cannot use timestamps to determine event boundaries. Ensure you have configured LINE_BREAKER or other event boundary settings.

suggestion.title: Consider adding TIME_PREFIX
suggestion.message: TIME_FORMAT is set but TIME_PREFIX is not defined. If your timestamp doesn't appear at the start of the event, adding TIME_PREFIX can improve timestamp extraction accuracy and performance.

suggestion.title: MAX_TIMESTAMP_LOOKAHEAD may be too low
suggestion.message: MAX_TIMESTAMP_LOOKAHEAD is set to a very low value. This limits how far into each event Splunk looks for a timestamp. If timestamps are not being extracted correctly, consider increasing this value.

suggestion.title: Low TRUNCATE value may cause data loss
suggestion.message: TRUNCATE is set below 10000 bytes. Events longer than this will be truncated, potentially losing important data. The default is 10000. Only lower this if you're certain your events are smaller.

suggestion.title: High TRUNCATE value may impact performance
suggestion.message: TRUNCATE is set above 100KB. Very large events can impact indexing performance and search speed. Ensure this is necessary for your data.

suggestion.title: Duplicate JSON extraction
suggestion.message: Both KV_MODE = json and INDEXED_EXTRACTIONS are set. This causes JSON fields to be extracted twice: once at index time and again at search time, impacting performance.

suggestion.title: Consider using REPORT for reusable extractions
suggestion.message: Inline EXTRACT is defined. For complex or reusable extractions, consider using REPORT-<class> with a transforms.conf stanza instead.

file_monitoring.description: Rules for file and directory monitoring

suggestion.title: Consider adding file filters
suggestion.message: This monitor input has no file filters (allowlist/denylist). For directories, consider adding filters to avoid indexing unwanted files like .gz, .tmp, or backup files.

suggestion.title: Consider setting explicit sourcetype
suggestion.message: No sourcetype is defined for this input. Splunk will attempt to auto-detect the sourcetype, which may not always be accurate. Consider setting an explicit sourcetype.

suggestion.title: Consider setting explicit index
suggestion.message: No index is specified. Data will go to the default index. For better data organization and access control, consider specifying an index.

suggestion.title: crcSalt and initCrcLength both set
suggestion.message: Both crcSalt and initCrcLength are configured. crcSalt=<SOURCE> is typically sufficient for handling files with identical content. Using both may be unnecessary.

suggestion.title: Consider setting connection_host
suggestion.message: No connection_host is set for this TCP input. By default, the host field will be set to the IP address. Consider setting connection_host = dns to use DNS names instead.

suggestion.title: Consider no_appending_timestamp setting
suggestion.message: For UDP inputs, Splunk appends a timestamp to each packet by default. If your data already has timestamps, consider setting no_appending_timestamp = true.

suggestion.title: Consider adding FORMAT for explicit field naming
suggestion.message: REGEX is defined without FORMAT. Field names will be derived from named capture groups in the regex. Adding FORMAT explicitly documents the field names and can make the configuration clearer.

suggestion.title: Consider adding default_match
suggestion.message: This lookup has no default_match configured. If a lookup key is not found, no fields will be added. Consider setting default_match to provide fallback values.

suggestion.title: Consider case_sensitive_match setting
suggestion.message: Lookup case sensitivity is not explicitly set. By default, lookups are case-sensitive. If your data has inconsistent casing, consider setting case_sensitive_match = false.

suggestion.title: DEST_KEY = queue requires FORMAT
suggestion.message: When routing events with DEST_KEY = queue, you must specify FORMAT to indicate the destination queue (indexQueue or nullQueue).

suggestion.title: Missing server setting
suggestion.message: This tcpout group has no server defined. At least one server must be specified for forwarding to work.

suggestion.title: SSL enabled without certificate path
suggestion.message: SSL is enabled but no certificate path is specified. Ensure sslCertPath and related SSL settings are properly configured.

suggestion.title: Replication factor of 1 provides no redundancy
suggestion.message: With replication_factor = 1, there is no data redundancy. If a peer fails, data may be lost. Consider increasing this for production environments.

suggestion.title: Consider separating hot/warm and cold storage
suggestion.message: For optimal performance, consider placing homePath (hot/warm) on faster storage (SSD) and coldPath on slower, cheaper storage.

suggestion.title: Consider setting maxDataSize
suggestion.message: maxDataSize is not explicitly set. The default is 'auto' which sets bucket size to 750MB. For high-volume indexes, consider 'auto_high_volume' for 10GB buckets.

suggestion.title: Consider setting retention policy
suggestion.message: No explicit retention policy is set. Data will be retained based on default settings. Consider setting frozenTimePeriodInSecs or maxTotalDataSizeMB to manage storage.
